en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Chattupāhanavagga 90.
The Training Rule on Having a Nun Massage One.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, nuns were having themselves massaged and rubbed by other nuns.
People, wandering on a tour of the monasteries, saw this and complained, grumbled, and spread it about:
"How can these nuns have themselves massaged and rubbed by other nuns, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can these bhikkhunīs have themselves massaged and have themselves rubbed by a bhikkhunī?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that nuns have nuns massage them and rub them down?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs have themselves massaged and rubbed by a bhikkhunī?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith...

And so, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should have herself massaged or rubbed by a bhikkhunī, that bhikkhunī is to be dealt with according to the rule."* (*The full penalty clause follows.)"
“Whichever nun, however, should have herself massaged or rubbed by another nun, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whichever nun” means whichever one of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Of a bhikkhunī":
"Of another nun":
if she causes herself to be massaged,
there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should have her rubbed" means she causes her to be massaged;
there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense—
For one who is ill,
in times of distress,
or for one who is insane.
"For one who is a first offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
